speaker: richard_field
text: A quire of the Rochelle crown, at the trade. Fourpence halfpenny, and I will not hear that it is a courtesy. It is the price. Sit, if thou canst sit, and chew on the side that still agrees with thee.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The right side agrees. The left is of another opinion, and the opinion is not invited. Fourpence halfpenny. I have it in the purse, not in a book.

speaker: richard_field
text: Then the purse may suffer, and the book may stay ignorant. Look at the stone. One turned letter, and a line dropped under it. A reader will not thank me for mending either. A reader will never know.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Show me the cost, then. I have been living as if a fault were a mood. I should like to see a fault that has weight.

speaker: richard_field
text: The forme comes unlocked. The line of type comes up in the fingers. The whole page is justified again, because one letter forgiven is a line that will not lock. Then a sheet is pulled, and the sheet is the only honest witness.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know this. A cue altered in one part is two other rolls altered, and I have been changing the king's rolls since July as if paper were weather.

speaker: richard_field
text: Thou changest a word and some poor devil copies three pages. Here it's my journeyman's morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I heard thee. I was about to say it myself, in worse words, and I am glad thou wert faster. The king has had too many of my mornings already.

speaker: richard_field
text: Then stop giving him mine. A turned letter is not a tragedy, Will. It is a morning. Tragedy is what thou wilt charge for on Thursday, and I hope the town pays thee better than a reader pays a corrected page.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The town pays what it pays. I am not bringing thee a sum from a playhouse. I am bringing thee fourpence halfpenny, and a confession that I have been a bad neighbour to my own book-keeper.

speaker: richard_field
text: Confess it to him, not to my type. My type is already tired of authors. Hold this sheet while I see whether the line sits. And do not improve it. Improvement is how a page learns to wobble.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will hold it. I will not improve it. Thou hast no idea how rarely I make that promise, and how poorly I have kept it since the spring.

speaker: richard_field
text: I have some idea. I have printed men like thee. They all think a second thought is a kindness. The kindness is leaving the sort alone once it locks.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: If both of you have finished discussing paper, one of you may move it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The pile is the point, then. We have been very grand beside it, and the passage is still shut.

speaker: richard_field
text: She is right, which I will not say often enough to become a habit. Take the near end. I have ink on the hand, and the ink is the valuable part of me this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The near end is mine. Mistress Field, tell us where it lives when it is no longer a sermon in the walkway.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Against the wall, clear of the bar. I would have moved it myself if either of you had left me a gap the width of a quire. You did not. So you will.

speaker: richard_field
text: There. The conversation may now become useful, which is a loss to literature and a gain to the house. What else dost thou want, besides the crown paper and the privilege of being scolded?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The paper, and the scolding, and nothing that has a price beyond fourpence halfpenny. I am not buying a lesson. Thou gavest it free, which is like thee and unlike a stall.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: He gave it because you were standing in the way of the press. Do not promote it to friendship until the sheet is dry. Friendship can wait on a damp proof.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will wait. The proof may teach me, and the proof will not flinch when I chew. Dick, the turned letter. Was it mine, in some copy of mine, or is this another man's weather?

speaker: richard_field
text: Another man's. Be grateful. Thine would have taken the morning and the moral with it. This one takes the morning only, and the moral thou mayst carry back to Shoreditch at no charge.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will carry it. A word changed here is a journeyman's morning. A word changed in a roll is three pages for a man who is not me. I have been pretending those were the same cheapness.

speaker: richard_field
text: They are not. Go and play thy king, or thy shrew, or whatever the afternoon has the cruelty to ask. Chew on the right. And take the quire before Jacqueline finds a second pile.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: There is no second pile, unless you make one by standing still. The door is behind you, Master Shakespeare. The paper is in your hand, if Richard has let go of it.

speaker: richard_field
text: I have let go. Fourpence halfpenny is on the nail, not in a ledger of mine. God keep thee. Try not to alter a locked line before dinner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: God keep thee. And thee, Mistress Field. I am moved. The pile is moved. The rest of the grandeur can stay on the stone, where it costs someone a real morning.
